Secondary growth occurs in roots and stems by the activity of cambium. Annual rings are distinct in most of the gymnosperm. 9. Gymnosperms are heterosporous, i.e. produces two types of spores (microspores and megaspores) inside sporangia. 10. The sporangia are developed on special leaf like structures, called sporophylls. 11. The sporophylls are aggregated to form cones or strobili. The cones are generally unisexual. 12. Pollination is anemophilous (i.e. pollination by wind). 13. Double fertilization is absent. 14. The life cycle shows alternation of generation. The sporophytic generation is dominant.
Examples: Pinus, Cycas, Ginkgo, Taxus, Ephedra, Juniper, etc.

Structure: Pinus are large, perennial and evergreen tall tree. It is worldwide in distribution mostly confined to northern hemisphere. They are mostly present in the temperate regions. The plant body is sporophyte. The plant bears longer branches towards the base and progressively shorter branches towards the upper region, giving a pyramid like appearance. The plant body is divided into root, stem and leaves. It has tap root system with lateral roots. The lateral roots are well developed and spread over a large area. The root hairs are replaced by mycorrhizal roots in older lateral root. In mycorrhizal root, there is a symbiotic association with fungi. The root helps in absorption and fixation. The stem is cylindrical, erect and remains covered with bark. The main trunk is unbranched. It has branches confined to the apical region. These branches form a characteristics canopy i.e. pyramid like appearance. The branches are dimorphic (i.e. two types of branches) - Branches of unlimited growth or long shoots which contain apical bud and grow indefinitely; whereas Branches of limited growth or dwarf shoots which are devoid of any apical bud, thus are limited in their growth. There are two types of leaves, the scale leaves and the green foliage leaves (modified as needles). The scale leaves are small, membranous and brownish in colour and are protective in function. They present in both long and dwarf shoot. The foliage leaves are green and needle like present in dwarf shoot only. The dwarf shoot with cluster of foliage leaves are known as ‘spurs’. The number of needles in each spur varies from species to species. The foliage leaves helps in photosynthesis.

Reproduction: Pinus are monocious (i.e. male and female reproductive organ developed in same individual). The male and female reproductive structures, known as cones or strobili develop on different branches of the same tree.
